learn.title: Signs in a product
learn.body: Multiplying integers uses two simple rules. Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer. Then multiply the sizes as usual.

learn.title: Why it works
learn.body: $3\times(-2)$ means 3 groups of $-2$, which is $-6$. Going the other way, $(-3)\times(-2)$ is the opposite of $3\times(-2)$. The opposite of $-6$ is $6$. Two negatives cancel out to a positive.

learn.title: Division follows the same rules
learn.body: Division undoes multiplication, so it has the same sign rules. $-36\div 9=-4$ because $-4\times 9=-36$. And $-20\div(-5)=4$ because $4\times(-5)=-20$.

learn.title: Work out $(-2)\times(-3)\times(-4)$
learn.body: Multiply two numbers at a time and watch the sign.
Count the negative signs in a product. An even count gives a positive answer, an odd count gives a negative one.

questions.explanation: Different signs, so the answer is negative: $4\times 6=24$, giving $-24$.
Same signs give a positive answer: $7\times 3=21$.
Different signs give a negative answer, and $36\div 9=4$.
Same signs give a positive answer: $20\div 5=4$.
Different signs: $9\times 8=72$, so the answer is $-72$.

questions.prompt: Match each product with its value.
questions.explanation: Same signs give a positive result. Different signs give a negative one. Three negative factors give a negative result.

questions.prompt: Work out $(-5)\times 4\div(-2)$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Work left to right. $-20$ divided by $-2$ has the same signs, so the result is positive: 10.
